description:
At 2 PM, Every CEO Dan Shipper had 30 emails in his inbox … and that basically never happens. In this video, he shows the Codex workflow that helped him hit inbox zero for 13 weeks straight: a Codex-native app that turns emails, Slacks, meetings, and company context into review cards, drafts next actions, and learns from every decision. It’s a look at Codex as an operating system for knowledge work.

Every is the most AI-native startup on the internet. Through ideas, software and education, subscribers get the tools to work at the frontier of AI. Start your free trial today: https://every.to/subscribe?utm_source=youtube

Follow Every: https://x.com/every
Follow Dan Shipper: https://x.com/danshipper

⌚ Timestamps:
00:00 Intro
01:09 The inbox card workflow
02:14 Turning company context into feeds
02:53 Queuing work for Codex
03:39 How Codex learns from decisions
04:16 Get this workflow + AI prompt

🔗 Links:
Try Cora to manage your inbox: https://cora.computer?utm_source=youtube

👇 Prompt to build your own AI inbox:
I want you to help me make an inbox sweep app. Here’s how it should work:
It should connect to my email. You can either use Cora’s CLI or Gmail; either one should work.
For every email that’s in my inbox, I want it to create a card that shows me what the email is about and then proposes a next action, whether that’s a draft reply or any other thing that makes sense.
It should allow me to scroll through my email and get through it just by talking to each card.
I want it to track every single step in the process, and it should be Codex native. That means the app should be responsible for the state, so all the state should be on the file system, and the app should be responsible for rendering the view. It should be built to be used inside of Codex in the in-app browser.
Can you build that end to end? I want you to set a goal with an unlimited budget, make sure the goal is really detailed, and include a set of validation steps where you step through it yourself to make sure that it works.
